threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'the Tube' instead of just 'the Overground'—you'll learn soon enough how important that distinction is round here.
Saw a guy on the 3 bus serenading everyone with a ukulele. By the time we hit Penge, half the bus was clapping along. Only in South London.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a guy selling homemade falafel from a bike, while a cat nonchalantly crossed the street, ignoring all the chaos.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find a kebab shop that doubles as an art gallery. Grab a döner and check out local artists’ work on the walls!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local if they can spot a fake taco truck from a mile away—ain't nothing worse than a tourist's Yelp review leading you astray.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading the 38 bus line with a ukulele yesterday. He stopped to let a lady with a cane board first. Classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always think Gràcia is just about Gaudí; they miss the hidden gardens where locals sip vermut in peace and share stories.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by how long they take to order a coffee. Locals know it’s 'café amb llet, to go' and not the full menu.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the overground is a train and not a rolling rave. Good luck finding a seat during peak hours!
Caught the 35 to Streatham last night, sat next to a guy in a full tuxedo who was holding a pizza box. Full-on wedding vibes at 2 AM, but he was just headed home.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I found a random street artist painting a mural of an old lady feeding pigeons while sipping a Berliner Kindl at Kottbusser Tor.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Kebab stand that serves currywurst on a bed of fries, topped with peanut sauce. It’s weirdly delicious.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their instinct to avoid the BART Civic Center stop. Loud bangs and smoke? Nah, we just take the bus or walk.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tattered suit serenading the bus stop with a trumpet. Bus rolled up, and it was clear no one wanted to interrupt the show.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals hang out in Plaça del Sol. The real vibe is at the little bars down side streets, where the conversations flow and the prices don't bite.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their confusion over whether to queue or just push past at the Mercat de Gràcia. The locals have their unspoken rules.
